reason: The quote and the mechanical claim are exact: MapRestoreManager.java:534-538 returns false before the journals.remove at line 540, so the journal survives and no RestoreOperation/activeRestores entry is created; ArenaInstance.reset() (ArenaInstance.java:1425, 1440-1446) sets restoreStarted=false and leaves state ENDING, and no code path transitions ENDING->WAITING except completeResetAfterRestore (1450-1463), so absent admin action the arena does stay in ENDING. However the impact sentence is refuted: the journal is deliberately preserved for retry (MapRestoreManagerTest.java:352-353 asserts that when the world is unavailable the journal must be preserved as-is so the next attempt can retry), and dropping it would make the documented recovery impossible. Recovery is not restart-only: disableArena (MultiArenaManager.java:459-462) -> ArenaInstance.stopGame() (774-777, scheduleReset) launches a delayed reset on the retired instance, and after the world is loaded again that reset re-enters restoreWithResult with the same journal and drains it; the GUI path ArenaResetService.reset likewise retries via restoreWithResult (369-370) and has an explicit not-loaded pre-check (271, 360-366) that keeps the arena DISABLED instead of wedging it. The failure is also loud, not silent: reset logs 'reset blocked ... run /hilltop disable ... then /hilltop enable ... to retry' (1443-1445), and the retained journal is size-capped at MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_PER_WORLD=1,000,000 (MapRestoreManager.java:106,357-365), not 'arbitrarily large'. Reachability is the weak link: the plugin never unloads worlds (no unloadWorld in src/main; ArenaResetService.java:600 states this assumption) and ArenaManager.ensureWorldsLoaded (214-247) plus MultiArenaManager.ensureWorldLoaded (398-411) guarantee the arena world is loaded before an ArenaInstance exists, so a null world at reset requires an external world-managing plugin (Multiverse) unloading/deleting an arena world in the few ENDING seconds - plausible but unusual, with no softdepend declared. Real residual defect: no automatic re-drive from the failure branch, so an external unload leaves the arena unavailable and up to ~170MB of journal resident until an admin acts. That is low severity, not medium.
